hero.lead: An island nation of 527,000 whose record tourism lifted growth to 6.3% in 2025, while public debt fell to 100.7% of GDP.

stats.label: IMF Extended Credit Facility, total access

record.text: Public debt, share of GDP, 2025, still falling; debt service takes 34.2% of government revenue (Cabo Verde Economic Update 2026, 14 July 2026)
IMF Extended Credit Facility, access of 220% of quota (SDR 52.14 million); Resilience and Sustainability Facility about $32.55 million; eighth review agreed at staff level on 8 May 2026
Real growth in 2025, supported by record tourist arrivals; near-term growth projected at around 4.7% (IMF staff, 8 May 2026)
Gross international reserves, end-2025, equal to 7.6 months of future imports (IMF staff, 8 May 2026)
Total expenditure in the amended 2026 State Budget, about €942 million, 8.6% above the budget first approved; approved 30 July and promulgated 12 August 2026

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · 220% of quota, SDR 52.14 million · seventh review completed 6 February 2026 · eighth review agreed at staff level 8 May 2026, subject to Executive Board approval
register.note: Board approval of the eighth review would release SDR 2.37 million (about $3.26 million)
register.text: Supports stronger public finances, debt sustainability and the reform of public enterprises. Staff and the authorities agreed the eighth review on 8 May 2026, after growth of 6.3% in 2025.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · 100% of quota, SDR 23.69 million · third review completed 6 February 2026 · fourth review agreed at staff level 8 May 2026, subject to Executive Board approval
register.note: Up to SDR 5.276 million (about $7.25 million) on Board approval, depending on reform progress
register.text: Climate resilience reforms for an island nation. Staff and the authorities agreed the fourth review on 8 May 2026.

register.name: Renewable Energy and Improved Utility Performance Project
register.detail: Announced 12 January 2026 · IDA concessional financing · co-financed by a $1.2 million concessional loan and a $0.41 million grant from the Canada Clean Energy and Forest Climate Facility, and a $0.4 million reimbursable grant from the Global Infrastructure Facility
register.note: 68 MW of new solar and wind, 12 MWh of battery storage and 1,800 household connections
register.text: Scales up support for new solar and wind generation and battery storage, with public investment on the smaller islands and private participation through a government-backed risk mitigation facility expected to mobilise $108 million of private capital. It also funds 1,800 more household connections and stronger water and power utilities, which serves the energy standard.
by: Canada Clean Energy and Forest Climate Facility

register.name: Development Policy Financing, third operation of the series
register.detail: Approved by the Board, announced 11 December 2025 · IDA credit · third operation in a programmatic series
register.note: Fiscal resilience; digitalisation and renewable energy; fisheries, tourism and women’s participation in the economy
register.text: Budget support on concessional IDA terms, tied to reforms in three pillars: fiscal resilience, digitalisation and renewable energy, and economic opportunities. They include climate risk assessments for public investment, universal electricity access and wider participation of women in the economy, which reach the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Blue Economy Sustainable Ports Facility, EU investment grant
register.detail: Signed 18 December 2025 · announced 16 January 2026 · EU grant managed by EIB Global · Global Gateway
register.note: The release gives 34 million euros; the EIB project page lists €33,333,333 signed
register.text: An EU grant that complements €114 million of EIB financing signed in 2024, in a package of about €148 million to rehabilitate and expand Cabo Verde’s main ports and its main shipyard. Works include a new breakwater and quay at Porto Grande in Mindelo and upgrades at Palmeira and Porto Novo, the ports through which food and goods reach the islands.

register.name: E-Governance and Public Financial Management Reform Programme, phase 2
register.detail: Approved by the Board, announced 3 December 2025 · loan, budget support · second phase
register.note: €17.71 million; a PEFA assessment is funded by the Middle Income Countries grant
register.text: Budget support for digital government and public finance reforms, including e-Justice to digitise judicial processes, a call for private operators at the technology park, and a plan to rationalise tax expenditures. Sound public finances pay for the schools, clinics and services behind the seven standards.

register.name: Blue Economy Sustainable Ports Facility, framework loan
register.detail: Approved 20 June 2024 · €80 million signed 2 September 2024 · €34 million signed 27 December 2024
register.note: Porto Grande (Mindelo), Porto Novo, Palmeira and the CABNAVE shipyard
register.text: An EIB framework loan to rehabilitate and expand ports across the archipelago and the main shipyard in São Vicente, to make them a regional centre of excellence. With the EU grant of December 2025 the package reaches about €148 million.

register.name: Cape Verde Green Energy framework loan
register.detail: Approved 28 November 2023 · €120 million signed 29 December 2023 · €23.6 million signed 11 September 2024 · works 2023 to 2029
register.note: Under the National Electricity Masterplan 2018–2040; total project cost €240 million
register.text: Finances linked generation, network and storage works under the National Electricity Masterplan, to help phase out the islands’ reliance on fossil fuels by 2040. The EIB release of 4 September 2024 presents €159 million of Team Europe support for this electricity system from the EIB, the EU and Luxembourg; it serves the energy standard.

register.name: Digital connectivity: submarine and inter-island cables
register.detail: Signed, announced 4 September 2024 · EIB financing with an EU financial guarantee · Global Gateway
register.note: A new submarine cable system linking Europe with the west coast of Africa, and a new fibre-optic cable between the islands
register.text: EIB financing, backed by an EU guarantee, to help the private sector and the country become a digital hub for West Africa. It funds a new submarine cable system and replaces the fibre-optic cable between the islands, connections on which digital public services and jobs depend.

register.name: Debt-for-climate conversion: Palmarejo solar plant
register.detail: Communiqué of 1 November 2024 · Cabo Verdean debt to Portugal converted into the Climate and Environmental Fund · plus €2 million of Cabo Verdean investment
register.note: Repowers the Palmarejo plant on Santiago from 4.4 MWp to 10 MWp
register.text: Under the debt conversion agreement signed by the two governments, Cabo Verdean debt to Portugal becomes investment through the Climate and Environmental Fund. This project, financed in full by the Fund, more than doubles the capacity of the Palmarejo solar plant on Santiago, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Cabo Verde Airports, second sustainability-linked loan
register.detail: Announced 4 February 2026 · loan of up to €60 million · three-year programme
register.note: Borrower: Cabo Verde Airports, a VINCI Airports subsidiary with a 40-year concession since 2023
register.text: IFC’s second sustainability-linked loan to the operator of the national airport network, for terminal expansions and upgrades at Sal, Praia, São Vicente, São Filipe, São Nicolau and Maio, a runway extension at Boa Vista, and new waste and wastewater treatment plants. Airports carry the visitors whose spending supports jobs and livelihoods across the islands.

register.name: Cabeólica wind expansion, EIB loan
register.detail: Release of 1 December 2025, at the inauguration of the new turbines and batteries · EIB Global loan of more than €39 million, backed by EU guarantees
register.note: Co-financed by the African Development Bank; the EIB first lent €28 million to Cabeólica in 2010
register.text: Finances the expansion of Cabeólica’s wind farms: 13.5 MW of new wind power on Santiago and 26 MWh of battery storage across four islands. Cabeólica already generates about 20% of the country’s electricity, a share expected to rise to 30%, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Cabeólica phase II, wind and battery storage
register.detail: Approved by the Board, announced 16 June 2025 · AfDB loan of about €12.6 million · SEFA concessional loan of about €7 million
register.note: 13.5 MW of wind and 26 MWh of battery storage on Santiago, Sal, Boa Vista and São Vicente
register.text: Finances the second phase of Cabeólica, the country’s first independent power producer, owned by Africa Finance Corporation, A.P. Moller Capital and Cabo Verdean public entities. It is expected to add over 60 GWh of clean energy a year, sold under a 20-year agreement with the national utility Electra.

register.name: Cabo Verde Airports, concession and refurbishment
register.detail: Signed 7 July 2023 · Proparco loan · alongside IFC and DEG
register.note: Supports 397 direct and 1,989 indirect jobs
register.text: Proparco’s loan, alongside IFC and DEG, financed the acquisition of the concession for Cabo Verde’s seven airports and refurbishment focused on safety and the environment. A fifth of Proparco’s financing brings climate co-benefits through renewable energy, LED lighting and new air-conditioning, and the project supports jobs, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Green Climate Fund readiness support
register.detail: Readiness grants approved 2021 to 2024 · including Enabling Direct Access to GCF Climate Finance for Cabo Verde (LuxDev, 5 February 2024)
register.note: Also blue economy capacities (FAO, 2021), country programming and sustainable tourism planning (UNIDO, 2022) and the RESIslands project (2024)
register.text: Grants that build Cabo Verde’s capacity to plan for and reach climate finance, from the blue economy and sustainable tourism to direct access to the Fund. They prepare the projects through which climate finance can reach water, energy and food on the islands.

register.name: Improving Connectivity and Urban Infrastructure, additional financing
register.detail: Approved 18 March 2026 · IDA · Two entries of $15 million and $10 million in the World Bank’s financial data · Project P178644
register.note: Additional financing; the project was first approved in 2022 at $40 million
register.text: Additional World Bank financing for climate-resilient roads on several islands, the upgrading of urban centres, neighbourhoods and waterfronts, and technical assistance. It serves the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Sixth Indicative Cooperation Programme, 2026–2030
register.detail: Signed February 2026 · Mindelo · Luxembourg grant programme “Partnership, Development and Resilience” · Education, employment, health, water and sanitation, climate action and energy transition
register.note: Raised from €75 million in the previous programme, according to the Government of Cabo Verde
register.text: Luxembourg’s five-year grant programme with Cabo Verde, implemented largely through LuxDev. It serves the education, water, health, energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Fifth Indicative Cooperation Programme, top-up
register.detail: Announced October 2025 · Luxembourg adds €17.6 million · Water and sanitation, vocational training and employment
register.note: Brings the 2021–2025 programme to about €116 million
register.text: An addition to Luxembourg’s fifth cooperation programme with Cabo Verde for water and sanitation and for vocational training and jobs. It serves the water and livelihood standards.

register.name: Debt-for-climate conversion, extension to 2030
register.detail: Announced 29 January 2025 · VII Portugal–Cabo Verde Summit, Lisbon · Ceiling raised from about €12 million to €42.5 million
register.note: New ceiling of Cabo Verdean debt to Portugal converted into the Climate and Environmental Fund by 2030
register.text: The Prime Minister of Portugal announced the tripling of the debt conversion, whose payments go into Cabo Verde’s Climate and Environmental Fund for renewable energy linked to water. It serves the water and energy standards; it extends the line of November 2024.

register.name: Development Policy Financing, second operation of the series
register.detail: Approved 12 December 2024 · IDA credit of about $1.3 million on small economy terms and $23.7 million on shorter maturity terms · Second of three
register.note: Budget support for fiscal consolidation and growth
register.text: The second operation in the World Bank’s Fiscal Space and Sustainable Growth series, supporting reforms to rebuild fiscal space, make public investment resilient to climate and improve state-owned enterprises. It frees budget room for the seven standards.

register.name: Resilient Tourism and Blue Economy, second additional financing
register.detail: Approved 30 April 2024 · IDA credit · Raises the project to $75 million
register.note: Second additional financing
register.text: IDA financing to make tourism more resilient and diversify the blue economy, the islands’ main source of jobs. It serves the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Growth in 2025, led by record tourism
items.text: Record arrivals already earn; the islands can price that demand into lasting infrastructure.
items.alt: A long white sand beach and turquoise sea below dry volcanic hills on Sal, Cabo Verde

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Wind and sun already supply part of the grid of a nation with no fuel of its own.
items.alt: Wind turbines and power lines on dry volcanic hills above the sea, Cabo Verde

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Green terraced fields of sugar cane and maize in a steep valley on Santo Antão, Cabo Verde

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Pine and cypress forest on misty mountain slopes, Cabo Verde

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 24.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A colourful street of the Plateau quarter in Praia, Cabo Verde, with people in the distance

items.name: Cabeólica
items.text: A wind power company whose four wind farms on different islands generate about 20% of Cabo Verde’s electricity. Its expansion, inaugurated in December 2025, added 13.5 MW of wind on Santiago and 26 MWh of battery storage across four islands.

items.name: Frescomar
items.text: A fish cannery in Mindelo working mainly with mackerel, tuna and bonito; its commercial director put its staff at 1,650 and its group at 80% of national exports.

items.name: Águas de Ponta Preta
items.text: A water company on Sal running a pilot, with Senegal’s Hérium, to remineralise water desalinated by reverse osmosis.

items.name: Health 360
items.text: A health-technology firm in Praia offering an integrated system to manage health services for municipalities, clinics and hospitals.

items.name: Morabi
items.text: A women’s association that lends small sums to women in business; in December 2018 it created Morabi, a savings and credit cooperative.
